epics.title: Project Management
epics.description: Project management features into the project.

tasks.title: Rename the task board to be the 'backlog'
there should be a tickbox next to each task that you want to confirm the agent to work on it
Generate workflows and each task should then follow a given workflow.
Schedule visualisation
tasks.description:
When a subtask is not scheduled, it is dimmed, but when it is, it is bright. You can then scroll along the timeline to see when the different tasks are scheduled. They then are green when completed, they are yellow and show a loading symbol when they are working, and they are blue when they have not yet been scheduled. 
You should be able to schedule tasks by clicking a cell on the time of a row. For example, for Epic A, task A, I should be able to click on a time on that row, and for that time to correspond to when the task is scheduled for.

tasks.title: Add a gantt chart functionality where each task can be assigned a time to build.
Add a kanban board functionality
Functional vs non-functional optional forcing
Include a robust way to stop the agent whilst it's processing.
Include a way to run agents on individual tasks.
Schedule at button for each task.
Import from github projects?
Workflow enhancement
tasks.description: The workflow currently supports a linear set of steps. However, it would be great if there was a node based interface option, that the user could prompt and generate structured workflows. I think this also has to be linear, but it could also have some form of conditions. IE: only continue when all previous unit tests have passed, or similar.

epics.title: Architecture
epics.description: Architecture is important to be able to understand a codebase and design implementation. I want to include a draw.io editor to store different architectures related to the codebase.

tasks.title: Implement the draw.io editor in the architectures window.
tasks.description: We need to use draw.io's embedded editor in the architecture window. There should be some default types of diagrams that the user is encouraged to draw, such as ERDs, flow diagrams, class diagrams and other SysML diagram types.

tasks.title: Agents need to track their own states by using one file (STATE.md). Each agent needs to read this before undertaking a task, and then update it once the task is complete.

There needs to be a mode wherein the agent operates autonomously, clearly stating the questions it comes up with and answers to it's own questions. The user can then see the reasoning the agent made in an overnight build.
Workflow steps need descriptions.
Adding skills via the skills thing.
Adding MCPs conveniently.
tasks.description: The workflows panel should include a section with mcp servers. The user should be able to conveniently add mcp servers into the workspace.

tasks.title: On startup, the agent should be able to infer the architecture of a project once it loads based on gathering it's context.
tasks.description: When loading a project, there should be a scan of the directory and the agent should infer the architecture of the software. The architectures should all be using draw.io and be in .xml format.

tasks.title: Find ways of tracking the token usage and API limits of each agent that the user has linked.
Common requirements documentation
tasks.description:
There should be a page dedicated to requirements tracking. Functional and non-functional. Each task in the backlog should be defined as containing functional, non-functional or both. The agent should then infer this upon invokation, and then they should update the requirements document accordingly. For example, if a user defines some functional requirements, the agent should then update the requirements doc with both functional and non-functional requirements. 

Further, the agent should then map these new requirements to the architecture document. The requirements doc and the architecture docs should be the common ground that all agents gather context on in order to develop robust solutions.

tasks.title: Handling blank projects
tasks.description: When a user starts overknight and it's in a blank project, the software should grant the user a textbox where they define their idea. From this, they define the tasks in the backlog, and some initial architectures and requirements. In the case the project is not empty, the action of getting the tasks in the backlog, generating the requirements doc and generating the architecture should be based on what the project already has.
